question: Do the exact positive and negative Stouffer step-wedge scans identify whether this historical flatbed workflow encodes optical transmittance, optical density, or only a separately calibrated monotone scanner response?

primary_sources.fact: ISO FDIS 14096-1 treats density range, density contrast sensitivity and characteristic transfer curve as separate digitizer measurements.

measurement.axis_rule: choose the image axis whose 21 equal-bin trimmed medians have the larger robust range; reject if the winning range is less than twice the other axis
measurement.orientation_rule: for each wedge independently choose the direction with the more negative Spearman correlation to the frozen increasing-density order; report the chosen reversal

branch_rule.parametric_pass: Retain only the winning measured scanner-code domain for this exact workflow and open a separately versioned bounded inverse primitive.
branch_rule.monotone_only_pass: Retain a scanner-specific monotone OECF requirement; do not label raw codes as transmittance or density.
branch_rule.fail: Close this exact wedge extraction/OECF route without changing bins, held steps, models or gates.

forbidden: infer film stock, camera exposure, development or colour response
generalize one scanner workflow to other scanners
tune extraction, split, models or thresholds after reading pixels
claim_ceiling: One CC-BY-4.0 historical flatbed scanner workflow step-wedge OECF measurement; not stock, emulsion, camera, process, colour, population or product calibration.
